summary: ECMP path rebalancing triggers HTTP/3 (QUIC) packet decryption failures for streaming responses in Private deployment
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports frequent failures for long-lived streaming responses when clients use HTTP/3 (QUIC) to the private deployment endpoint. Failures start ~30-90s into a stream and manifest as QUIC packet decryption errors and abrupt stream termination. Impact: Active users in production experience broken streaming completions for chat/streaming endpoints; user-facing error rate ~8% for affected customers, causing perceived instability in product demos.

Environment: Private deployment in Acme Ads' VPC peered to Redwood Private control plane via Transit Gateway. Traffic path includes customer on-prem -> transit GW -> redundant DirectConnect links -> cloud TGW -> Redwood VMs behind GWLB. ECMP is enabled across two upstream transit links. QUIC/HTTP3 is allowed through firewalls and load balancers.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Client establishes HTTP/3 connection to private endpoint and begins a streaming completion.
2) Stream proceeds normally for ~30-90s with many packets exchanged (large responses, long-lived).
3) Suddenly client logs show QUIC error: PACKET_DECRYPTION_FAILURE / CRYPTO_ERROR and stream terminates; server records connection close with QUIC_ERROR(0x1d).
4) Restarting client session usually succeeds for a short period then may fail again after similar duration.

Observed logs and captures: 
- Server-side QUIC logs: "connection 0x7f...: received undecryptable packet, dropping (PACKET_DECRYPTION_FAILURE)" (multiple occurrences).
- Client debug: "quic: received PACKET_DECRYPTION_FAILURE, stateless reset?"
- tcpdump from customer edge shows significant packet reordering and out-of-order UDP datagrams for the same QUIC connection around the failure window (sequence gaps and >200ms reorder).
- VPC flow logs and traceroute show that traffic for the same 5-tuple is traversing two different upstream physical links after a transient ECMP hashing change correlated with a load rebalancing event on the transit router.

Hypothesis: QUIC is sensitive to packet reordering and path rebalancing; ECMP across unequal-latency/congestion paths is causing reordering/out-of-order delivery leading to QUIC decryption errors because packet-level reassembly/crypto state gets disrupted. Traditional TCP streams tolerate reordering; QUIC (UDP + crypto) exhibits packet drop/decrypt failures under this pattern. The rebalancing appears tied to transit gateway flow hashing when upstream link metrics changed.

Investigation notes: 
- Reproduced with tcpdump and pcap analysis from customer edge and Redwood egress node; timestamps show packets for the same connection arriving at different egress points with >100ms skew.
- No signs of middlebox tampering or SNI stripping; TLS cert validation passes on fresh connections.
- When customer temporarily forced a single egress path (disabled one DirectConnect), QUIC streams remained stable for the same traffic and load pattern.

Impact assessment: Affects customers using HTTP/3/QUIC to private endpoints or going through multi-path ECMP topologies. Streaming completions are most impacted (long-lived flows). Not all customers are affected — those with single-path or consistent per-flow hashing see no issues.

Temporary workaround applied: Support requested customer to pin egress to a single active path (disabled one DirectConnect) and asked Redwood to apply similar per-flow affinity at gateway where possible. Workaround reduced observed failures to ~0.2% during test window.

Next steps / remediation plan: 
- SRE: propose configuration change on Redwood transit routers/GWLB to prefer per-flow hash that uses 5-tuple rather than symmetric hashing that can flip on path metric changes. (Assigned INT-4021).
- Support: coordinate with customer networking team to avoid transient ECMP rebalancing during peak usage windows.
- Product: add a note to Private deployment networking guide warning about QUIC sensitivity to ECMP rebalancing and recommend sticky egress or single-path for high-stability streaming.
- Engineering: evaluate adding more tolerant QUIC implementation knobs (reordering thresholds, larger decryption window) in serving runtime if safe.

References: PCAP excerpts, VPC flow logs and traceroute attached to ticket (see links in comments).
